spec.description: USE-shaped host view for on-call: utilisation, saturation and errors for CPU, memory, filesystem and network on each Proxmox node.

spec.title: Load / core
spec.description: 1-minute load average divided by core count. Above 1.0 the run queue is longer than the machine can service.

spec.title: Swap
spec.description: Swap in use. Sustained swapping on a hypervisor means guests are being starved.

spec.title: CPU Utilisation
spec.description: Threshold band painted at 90%.

spec.title: Load Average
spec.description: Raw load averages against the core count. Crossings of the 'cores' line are the thing to watch.

spec.title: CPU by Mode
spec.description: Where CPU time actually goes, derived from the cpustat_*_total jiffies counters (rate / 100 / cores). Proxmox reports guest time as a peer of user, not nested inside it, so all bands sum to ~1.0. Stacked, unsmoothed.

spec.title: I/O Wait
spec.description: TRAP: despite the _total suffix this metric is a GAUGE, not a counter -- it is non-monotonic (verified 0.0008-0.0072 over 6h). Never rate() it. Sustained high values mean storage is the bottleneck.

spec.title: Host vs Guest CPU
spec.description: How much of the machine the guests are actually taking, versus hypervisor overhead and headroom.

spec.expr: (sum by (node) (rate(proxmox_node_cpustat_user_total{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / 100 / on (node) sum by (node) (proxmox_node_cpustat_cpus{node=~"$node"})) + (sum by (node) (rate(proxmox_node_cpustat_system_total{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / 100 / on (node) sum by (node) (proxmox_node_cpustat_cpus{node=~"$node"}))

spec.title: vCPU Overcommit
spec.description: Sum of vCPUs assigned to running guests divided by physical cores. Above 1.0 is normal and fine; above ~4.0 on a busy node is where scheduling latency starts to bite.

spec.expr: sum by (node) (proxmox_vm_cpus{node=~"$node"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node"} > 0) / on (node) sum by (node) (proxmox_node_cpustat_cpus{node=~"$node"})

spec.title: Load vs CPU
spec.description: Every sample in the range plotted as load-per-core against CPU utilisation. On a CPU-bound host the points track the diagonal. Points sitting well ABOVE it are the interesting case: the run queue is long while the CPU is not busy, which means tasks are blocked in uninterruptible I/O sleep -- Linux counts those in load average but not in CPU time. That is a storage problem wearing a CPU problem's clothing, and no single-metric panel can show it.

spec.title: Memory Composition
spec.description: Stacked to the physical total. 'available' is shown separately below because it overlaps free + reclaimable cache.

spec.title: Available Memory
spec.description: MemAvailable is the honest 'how much can I still allocate' number -- it counts reclaimable page cache, which memfree does not.

spec.title: RAM Overcommit
spec.description: RAM promised to running guests divided by physical RAM. Above 1.0 the node depends on ballooning or swap to keep its promises.

spec.expr: sum by (node) (proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node"} > 0) / on (node) sum by (node) (proxmox_node_memory_memtotal{node=~"$node"})

spec.title: ZFS ARC
spec.description: The ZFS adaptive replacement cache against the bounds it is allowed to move between. ARC is counted as used memory by Proxmox, but everything above `min` is reclaimable under pressure -- so a host sitting at its ARC max is not short of memory in the way the headline figure suggests. Sitting at `min` while memory is tight is the case worth investigating.

spec.title: ARC Share of RAM
spec.description: How much of the host's RAM the ARC currently holds. Most of it is reclaimable, so this is context for the memory headline rather than a problem on its own.

spec.title: Root FS Inodes
spec.description: Inode exhaustion fills a filesystem that still reports free bytes. Usually caused by huge numbers of tiny files.

spec.title: Root FS Capacity
spec.description: Note: 'used' + 'available' is less than 'total' -- the difference is space reserved for root (typically 5%).

spec.title: Root-Reserved Space
spec.description: Proxmox exposes two views of the same filesystem: su_* (what a superuser can consume) and user_* / bare (what an unprivileged process can). The gap is the reserve that keeps the node bootable when the disk fills.

options.content: Proxmox reports **every** interface under the same `device` label — physical NICs, bridges (`vmbr*`), and one tap/veth pair per guest NIC. Summing them all triples real traffic, so each panel below filters to one class.

spec.title: Physical NICs
spec.description: Real traffic entering and leaving the host. Transmit is negated so the two directions mirror around zero.

spec.title: Bridges
spec.description: Traffic crossing the Linux bridges. Guest-to-guest traffic appears here but not on the physical NICs.

spec.title: Busiest Interfaces
spec.description: Total throughput per interface, all classes. Neutral ranking -- a flat colour, because 'busiest' is not 'worst'.

spec.title: Guest Interfaces (tap/veth)
spec.description: Per-guest virtual NICs. The number in tapNNNiX / vethNNNiX is the vmid.

spec.title: Proxmox VE · Node Operations
